_meta.section: Spiritual Gems Q1 — Isa 59:11 'keep growling like bears' + supporting verses
_meta.preparation_standard: Q1 anchors to v11. Supporting underlines on v1 (Jehovah's reach), v2 (the actual barrier), v17 (warrior imagery). Two notes — v11 (the bear-dove warning) + v1 (the reach is not too short).

notes.content: Look at how the chapter opens. 'Look! The hand of Jehovah is not too short to save.' Notice the negative framing — Jehovah isn't telling us his hand IS reaching, he's telling us it's NOT too short. Why phrase it that way? Because that's the lie we believe. When something heavy is happening, our default thought is, 'maybe he can't reach me from where I am.' Verse 1 walks straight into that thought and corrects it. The reach is not the problem. Then verse 2 says what IS — our own offenses are the wall. The distance isn't on Jehovah's end. It never was.

underlines.phrase: the hand of Jehovah is not too short
his ear too dull to hear

notes.content: You ever notice some people who complain a lot, but never actually try to fix anything? Bears growl when something's wrong. Doves coo when they're mourning. Both sounds — frustration, sadness — but neither one does anything about the cause. Verse 11 says the Israelites kept growling and kept cooing, hoping for justice. Then look at the very next verse — verse 12 — 'our offenses are many before you, and our sins testify against us.' Their sins were the very thing keeping justice far. The bear-and-dove problem isn't that they're upset. It's that they're upset about something they're causing themselves and won't address. Sometimes the growling is the warning — about what's in us.

underlines.phrase: We all keep growling like bears
We hope for justice, but there is none
righteousness like a coat of mail
